helpHint.message: Getting started, features, and common questions.

helpIntro.message: Get started with JustOneHop’s core features, shortcuts, and interaction model. View the complete illustrated guide on GitHub.

fullGuideDesc.message: Includes comprehensive guides, complete shortcut cheat sheets, Tab Switcher advanced setup, and illustrations.

helpStartBody.message:
• Open palette: Click the JustOneHop toolbar icon or press the launch shortcut to open the palette (current: $1).
• Change shortcut: Change the shortcut in Settings → Keyboard, or right-click the toolbar icon to edit the binding or open this guide in a new tab.

helpSearchBody.message:
• Unified search: Search tabs, bookmarks, commands, and settings in one place using English or Chinese keywords, without mode prefixes. Combine page titles, domains, tab groups, or bookmark folders in any order—for example, “new tab”, “reopen last tab”, “theme”, or “downloads”.
• Open options: Bookmarks and history open in the current tab with Enter or a click. Command+Enter on macOS or Alt+Enter on Windows/Linux opens a new active tab; the footer and Actions menu offer both choices. Pinned source tabs only allow a new tab; open-tab results still switch to that tab.
• History search: Browsing history from the past week joins search results. Search All History appears seventh, or at the end of shorter lists, to search all time. A slow history query does not block other results; late replies do not insert rows.
• Smart ranking: Main search and Search All History apply habits only within the same relevance tier for the same query, show a history icon for remembered preferences. Successfully opened history results share preferences with tabs at the same website address. Hover or focus the icon to see why and what will be forgotten; click it to forget, or press Shift+Backspace on the selected result (affects both history and tab results).
• Recommendations: The empty home shows up to 10 suggested pages and commands based on successful use in JustOneHop, with curated commands when there is little history. Recommendations keep their order until the next opening.

helpAddressBody.message:
• Go to URL: Type a web address, domain, or localhost to show “Go to URL” as the first result (unless matching tabs, bookmarks, or history already contain the exact address; differing path, params, or fragments are treated as distinct). Press Enter or click to navigate in the source tab; Command+Enter on macOS or Alt+Enter on Windows/Linux opens and activates a new tab in the same window (HTTPS by default, HTTP for localhost). Pinned source tabs only allow opening in a new tab; only HTTP(S) targets are supported.
• Google search: Non-empty queries offer “Search Google for ‘keywords’” after local matches (or as first item if there are no local matches). Type google React hooks to pin Google search to top. Supports the same current tab and new tab shortcuts.
• Local & private: Search typing stays 100% on device; only selected Google results open the web search page (no online suggestions, extra permissions, or telemetry).

helpControlsBody.message:
• Actions menu: Right-click a result, click Actions in the footer, or press Cmd/Ctrl+K to open actions for the selected item (copy URL, pin, mute, close, etc.).
• Keyboard navigation: Lists support Ctrl+P (previous) and Ctrl+N (next) alongside the arrow keys.

helpBackBody.message:
• Going back: Press Esc, click the back arrow, or press Backspace in an empty secondary search field to return one level with your search and selection restored. At the main search, Esc closes JustOneHop.
• Swipe back: Swipe horizontally in the back direction inside the panel (commonly two fingers swiping right with macOS natural scrolling). When the blue arrow appears, child views return immediately; scrolling settles before closing the main search or standalone Help. Horizontally scrollable text areas do not trigger this.

helpTabsBody.message:
• Manage tabs: Pinning, muting, and closing other tabs keep the palette open for continued cleanup. Bulk close preserves pinned tabs. Closing the tab you opened JustOneHop from ends the palette session.
• Tab groups: Search a tab group’s name to manage its tabs (expand/collapse, rename, ungroup, or close group).
• Tab Switcher: Choose JustOneHop: Tab Switcher to filter recent tabs inside the palette, then click a row or press Enter to switch; Cancel returns to your search. When launching the switcher with its shortcut, hold the modifier key to select and release to switch; click the search field or press Cmd/Ctrl+F to pause release-to-switch and filter by text instead.

helpTuckBody.message:
• Tuck away tabs: “Tuck Away Tab” moves a tab into a collapsed group at the end of the window without closing or discarding it; switch to the tab from search anytime to bring it back.
• Auto tuck tabs: Turn on in Settings to choose how long tabs can remain unused before tucking (1/3/12 hours or 1/3/7 days; 7 days by default). Checks run every 5 minutes and when your computer becomes idle. Turning this off returns all still-managed tabs, including manually tucked tabs.
• Recover tucked tabs: If a group needs confirmation after a browser restart, search for “recover tucked tabs”.

helpStorageBody.message:
• View website storage: Search for “local storage”, “session storage”, or “cookies” on a webpage. Select a key on the left to preview its value on the right; JSON is formatted for reading, and storage is read-only.
• Copy value: Press Enter or click Copy Value to copy the original string.
• Cookie access: Reading cookies requests permission only for the current site’s domains, which you can revoke anytime in Chrome’s extension settings.

helpShortcutBody.message:
• Shortcut configuration: If a shortcut is unassigned or conflicts, open Settings → Keyboard to change it in Chrome’s extension shortcuts page.
• Ctrl+Tab setup: Due to browser limits, Ctrl+Tab requires one-time manual setup—search for “ctrl tab” for the setup code and steps.

helpWindowBody.message:
• Overlays and windows: JustOneHop keeps an in-page overlay on ordinary webpages, even when the address bar has focus. Chrome internal pages and pages that cannot host the overlay use a separate window.
• Restoring focus: If typing is unavailable because the address bar holds focus, click the search field.

helpPrivacyBody.message:
• 100% Local & private: JustOneHop has no account, server, or telemetry. Preferences and learned search ranking stay on your device; website storage values stay only in the current panel’s memory. Incognito windows do not read ordinary history or record selections.
• Browsing history: Browsing history requires the history permission at installation. JustOneHop keeps no persistent copy of the history database; it remembers only search terms and website addresses you explicitly select and successfully open.
• Full guide on GitHub: Detailed documentation, guides, and releases are open source on GitHub (lyyourc/JustOneHop).
